newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian army destroys Christian-run centre.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian army destroys Christian-run centre.

text.p: The Egyptian army has destroyed a half-built Christian institute for handicapped children outside Cairo, sources close to the institute said on Wednesday.
The Coptic Christian charity which runs the institute has complained to the authorities about the incident in December but has not yet received a reply, added the bishop in charge.

"The army brought bulldozers and other equipment and razed the buildings to the ground. Some of them were three-storey buildings. They will have to restart from scratch," said one source who saw the site both before and after the incident.
The buildings, about 25 km (15 miles) northeast of Cairo, were meant to provide more space for children in the care of the Cheerful Heart Centre for the Mentally Disabled.
Bishop Botros, chairman of the board of the St John the Divine Institution for Development and Social Services, told Reuters he did not know what the army's motive might have been.
"I have no idea. We have had no reply from any quarter," said the bishop, whose institution runs the centre.
The centre is close to military bases but the bishop denied there was any dispute over the land. The centre cares for children of all religions.

The authorities have recently demolished many buildings in the Cairo area because the owners did not have licences to build. But the bishop said this could not have been the motive. "I have all licences, no problem with licences," he said.
